context: Proof of Theorems 4 and 5. The lower bounds in both theorems follow from Lemmas 7 and 9, since drops(σd ) = d/2 for σd as defined in (3). The proof of the upper bounds is by induction and is not presented due to space considerations. J Remarks First, none of the bounds in Theorem 5 is tight for all k. For example, the 2drops(k) upper bound exceeds the upper bound from Theorem 4 for k = σd from (3). Furthermore, we do not know which of the bounds in Theorem 4 is more accurate. Second, we have eipTd (σd ) ≤ d/2 − Ω(log d). Hence, the lower bound of drops(k) − O(log(drops(k)) from Theorem 5 cannot be improved as a function of drops(k). A similar statement holds for Lemma 7 and sbl(k). Third, the quantity st(k) from Claim 8 characterizes eip almost exactly: st(k) − 1 ≤ eipTd (k) ≤ st(k). This can be deduced from Claim 8 and Theorem 2.3 from [3]. It also implies |eipTd (k) − sbl(k)| ≤ O(log k).
